retractedFinding.effect: E4-R3 has no dead-pin defect. No corrective commit was requested of the lane, and none is owed.

confidenceAdjudications.question: Demote to still_blocked unless the exact license passes.
confidenceAdjudications.licenseRule: A compiled pathway that alters only the waiting period for an offence class, and files the same petition, maps to the registry track that owns that petition.

line 14 states DWI 'is carved out of the ordinary waiting-period structure', i.e. a period variant, not a separate petition vehicle

discriminator holds: nh_conviction_streamlined carries only RSA 651:5 III(a)(2) and III(b)(2), the short mandatory route for violations and Class B misdemeanours, which cannot host a pathway defined by a 10-year carve-out
confidenceAdjudications.residual: The exact paragraph of RSA 651:5, III carrying the carve-out is not pinned in this repository. The lane declared this residual itself; it is why the row is medium, not a reason the mapping fails.

collisionAdjudications.reasoning: dismissal-or-quash is the primary mapping by name identity with the registry legalName 'Expunction where the charge was dismissed or quashed'. class-c-deferred is a compiled VARIANT: a Class C deferred disposition is the express exception written into the community-supervision bar at art. 55A.051(3), which is tx_exp_dismissed's own authority, not an independent article. A variant does not add a track to the denominator.
collisionAdjudications.residual: Whether a Class C deferred disposition counts as court-ordered community supervision for the art. 55A.051(3) carve-out is an open ELIGIBILITY question the registry itself flags. It does not disturb the mapping: either way the pathway lives inside art. 55A.051. Routed to counsel.

collisionAdjudications.reasoning: Both tracks are petitions under Md. Crim. Proc. § 10-105, so a single compiled pathway covering § 10-105 can legitimately host both. The pinned registry confirms both trackIds exist and are distinct petitions (favorable-disposition vs post-pardon).
collisionAdjudications.residual: A pardon-based expungement and a favorable-disposition expungement are different eligibility gates sharing a statute. Collapsing them onto one pathway may erase a distinction a participant depends on. Counsel must confirm the pathway genuinely covers both entry routes.

collisionAdjudications.reasoning: W. Va. Code § 61-11-26 carries all three conviction classes in one section, so one compiled pathway over that section can host all three registry tracks.
collisionAdjudications.residual: The three tracks carry materially different waiting periods and eligibility bars. A single pathway must express those differences or it will misprice eligibility for two of the three. Highest-risk collision of the four.

collisionAdjudications.reasoning: Both are felony expungement routes under KRS 431.073, which the compiled pathway names.
collisionAdjudications.residual: Post-pardon and post-vacatur are distinct predicates. Counsel must confirm KRS 431.073 is the operative vehicle for both rather than one being a separate mechanism.
